**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding**: no documented flow from signup → first class → habit formation (induction safety checks, goal capture, buddy assignment, week-1 touchpoint missing)
- **Churn & Win-back**: no process for pause requests, cancellation reasons capture, or re-engagement triggers
- **Coaching Standards & QA**: no class quality audit, coach feedback loop, or consistency framework across instructors
- **Health & Safety / Incident Management**: no complaint logging, injury reporting, or escalation protocol (critical for liability)
- **Finance & Admin**: no supplier ordering process, invoice approval, or payment reconciliation documented
- **Member Data & GDPR**: no data handling, consent, retention, or deletion SOP (legal exposure)
- **Referral & Milestone Tracking**: no structured way to capture referrals, reward them, or celebrate member wins (retention lever you're missing)

- **Coach SOPs (18/21)**: missing weekly task assignment, development roadmap, and 1:1 feedback cadence — coaches likely operating ad-hoc

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your wishlist.** Audit what your coaches actually deliver right now (group classes, 1:1 PT, nutrition plans, challenges, etc.). Price based on what you're *consistently* selling, not what sounds good. This prevents menu bloat and coach confusion.

• **Create TWO documents, not one.** Coaches need a pricing/commission structure (what they earn per service, upsell triggers). Members need a clean visual menu showing class types, PT packages, and add-ons. Different audiences = different info density.

• **Build a simple decision tree for pricing tiers.** For PT specifically: e.g., "4-pack (drop-in rate) vs. 8-pack (10% discount) vs. unlimited monthly." This nudges members toward higher-value packages without overwhelming choice. Same logic for any membership add-ons.

• **Lock in ONE person as "menu owner" (probably you).** Give coaches 1 week to flag what's missing or broken, then finalize. Otherwise you'll be re-writing it every month. Make it live on your website, in-gym, and in your booking system simultaneously—no version confusion.

• **Test pricing on your most loyal members first.** Before rolling out publicly, get feedback from 3-5 regulars. They'll spot if something doesn't make sense or if pricing feels off. One conversation beats guessing.

What's your current pricing situation—are you charging at all for PT right now, or starting from scratch?
